documents.purpose: Hapke law Helfenstein, Hillier, Weitz and Veverka fitted to Voyager and Earth-based photometry of Oberon, used to light the globe.

references.evidence: Pages 230 and 231, the authors' summary of the study later published in Icarus 90, 14 (1991), which was not read. It says Hapke's (1986) model was fitted to Voyager imaging and Earth-based photometry of Oberon, and that the phase coverage constrains all five parameters only in the clear filter (0.48 micrometres). Table I, Global Average, Clear: single-scattering albedo 0.41, Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry -0.29, macroscopic roughness 21 degrees; its footnote gives the opposition surge width h = 0.007 and amplitude B0 = 1.03. Those five numbers are the record's model, with the H-function of Hapke's 1981 to 1986 papers. The table's terrain rows (average cratered, bright craters, dark materials) were fitted to resolved images. The report states no phase or emission range. The record's phase range, 18 to 148 degrees, is derived here: it is the span of the Voyager 2 frames in which the PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node lists Oberon at 10 pixels radius or more; the fit also used Earth-based photometry nearer opposition.
references.locator: Pages 230 and 231, Helfenstein, Hillier, Weitz and Veverka, Oberon: color photometry and its geological implications; Table I

references.evidence: The fitted emission limit, 84.9 degrees, is derived here, not printed: it is the emission angle at the outermost pixel centre of the clear frame the report names as its highest resolution, FDS 26836.25 (C2683625), on a 761.4 km sphere, arcsin((R - 0.5 pixel)/R). The PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node lists its centre resolution as 6.13035 km per pixel and its phase as 38.9 degrees; the whole disc is in the frame.

documents.credit: Paul Helfenstein, John Hillier, Catherine Weitz and Joseph Veverka, Reports of Planetary Geology and Geophysics Program 1989 (NASA TM-4210), pages 230 and 231. Transcription, phase range and emission limit: cssEarth.
documents.acquisition: Parameters transcribed from the report's Table I into a project document; the phase range and emission limit are computed from what the PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node lists; no data file was downloaded.
